title: OTLP concordance layer for KV-cache telemetry and per-request KPI mapping
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need a lightweight OTLP "concordance" layer that reconciles incoming traces and OTLP metrics into deterministic per-request inference KPIs. Current telemetry ingestion provides raw spans and Prometheus-style metrics but lacks a stable mapping from a trace/span to the derived KPI labels we surface in dashboards (model, route, cache_hit, kv_prefix_shard, batch_size). This gap causes noisy cardinality and makes error/latency investigation expensive. The concordance layer will: 1) consume OTLP traces and aggregated metrics, 2) resolve KV cache hits/misses by matching span events and request envelopes, 3) emit normalized KPI envelopes with canonical labels suitable for Prometheus rollups and downstream SLO computation, and 4) provide a labeled fallback when trace linkage is missing (best-effort deterministic heuristics).
technical_approach: 1) Ingest: Deploy a small stateless OTLP consumer (go) fronting the existing telemetry gateway. It subscribes to span streams and a lightweight metric delta feed. 2) Key-resolution: Use span attributes (request_id, tenant_id, model_ref, route) + inferred prefix hash to synthesize a concordance key. 3) KV cache detection: Parse span events for 'kv-cache.hit' / 'kv-cache.miss' markers inserted by the runtime; fallback to delta counters when events are absent. 4) Envelope emission: Produce a structured KPI envelope (OTLP metric or push to a Kafka topic) with normalized labels: model, route, tenant, cache_status, prefix_bucket, batch_size, inference_path. 5) Prometheus compatibility: A downstream adapter converts KPI envelopes to Prometheus histograms/gauges and writes to the scraper endpoint. 6) Cardinality control: Apply configurable bucketization for prefix_bucket and max-label cardinality per tenant with sampling for noisy tenants. 7) Backfill/Replay: Support replay from raw span logs to reconstruct missing mappings for backfill and evals.
acceptance_criteria: Concordance layer deployed behind telemetry gateway and receiving OTLP spans in staging.
KPI envelopes contain canonical labels (model, route, tenant, cache_status, prefix_bucket, batch_size) for >= 95% of traced requests in staging.
Prometheus downstream shows per-route latency histograms and cache_hit ratio stable against known baseline within 5% delta.
Cardinality protection prevents >2x label explosion for noisy tenants in synthetic stress test.
End-to-end test-run (sample load) correlates a traced high-latency request to the exact KPI row in dashboards and gives correct KV-cache status.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Enable concordance consumer for a small subset of tenants and plumber test traffic. Validate label synthesis and KV events mapping.
Phase 2 (gradual): Route 10%, 25%, 50% production traffic with feature flag. Monitor cardinality and ingestion rate. Enable sampling for top noisy tenants.
Phase 3 (full): Promote to default path for all telemetry and switch downstream dashboards to canonical KPI source. Keep old metrics as fallback for 2 weeks.
Rollback: Disable concordance consumer and revert dashboards to previous aggregated metrics. Keep replay process to repair any missed mappings.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Label cardinality explosion from free-form route/model tags. Mitigation: enforce schema and bucketize prefix labels with configurable hash buckets.
Risk: Increased ingestion load causing gateway backpressure. Mitigation: consumer is stateless and autoscaled; add backpressure signals and degrade to sampled concordance when under strain.
Risk: Mismatched mapping when spans are dropped. Mitigation: best-effort heuristics + replay/backfill via raw logs and delta counters to reconstruct missing KPI rows.
Risk: Incorrect KV-cache inference for legacy runtimes. Mitigation: coordinate a small runtime change to emit explicit kv-cache.* span events; add backwards-compatible counter heuristics.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests: concordance key derivation, prefix bucketization, label sanitization.
Integration tests: end-to-end from runtime -> telemetry gateway -> concordance -> prometheus adapter using synthetic traces including KV hit/miss events.
Load test: 10k req/s synthetic workload validating throughput and backpressure behavior; verify <1.5x increase in telemetry ingress CPU.
Regression test: compare latency histograms before/after on canary tenants; no regressions >5%.
Canary dashboard: live debug panel that maps trace IDs to KPI envelopes with sample links to the original span.
